product.name: Kaku
product.tagline: A fast, out-of-the-box macOS terminal built for AI coding.
product.description: Kaku is a macOS-native terminal emulator derived from WezTerm and tuned for AI-assisted terminal work. It ships practical defaults on day one (JetBrains Mono, macOS font rendering, automatic dark and light themes), fast tabs and split panes on native macOS shortcuts, a curated shell suite (Lazygit, Yazi, remote files, z, completion, syntax highlighting), and a built-in assistant that drafts a fix when a command fails and turns plain language into commands. It keeps full Lua API compatibility with WezTerm, so existing configs work with no migration.

api.reason: Kaku is a local macOS application, not a service. There is no HTTP API, no SDK, no MCP server, and no server-side product. Automation goes through the local `kaku` command.

authentication.note: Kaku has no account system and no credentials to obtain. The optional AI assistant uses an API key that the user supplies for their own OpenAI-compatible provider; that key stays in ~/.config/kaku/assistant.toml on the user's machine.

whenToUse: Set up a macOS terminal that works immediately, without an afternoon of configuration.
Terminal work alongside AI coding, where the AI stays optional and talks only to a user-configured provider.
Replace iTerm2 with something lighter, or replace Warp without a cloud account.
Reuse an existing WezTerm Lua config with better defaults and no migration.
Privacy-sensitive setups: no telemetry, no account, and every network call documented at https://kaku.fun/privacy.
whenNotToUse: Windows or Linux targets: unsupported, no date promised.
Any integration that needs a network API, SDK, or hosted tool endpoint.

install.homebrewNote: Use the tap package. The unrelated Homebrew `kaku` package is a different project.
